extracted.intended_audience: federal contracting officers, procurement professionals, and agency acquisition managers
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and recommendations for determining whether a commercial or industrial type activity should be performed in-house by Government personnel or contracted to private sources under OMB Circular A-76, plus field-level recommendations for contracting practice and implementation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation 1
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracting Officers consider the determination of the availability of commercial sources to be one of their primary responsibilities under the new Circular guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Early participation by contracting personnel in the assessment phase of the CITA cycle should help achieve this objective; development of sources of supply traditionally centers on contracting expertise.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation 2
rubrics_metrics.description: Informational solicitations be used, if at all, only in conjunction with other required methods for determining potential private sector interest in a CITA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If no commercial interest is expressed from an informational solicitation alone, Commerce Business Daily (CBD) notices are still required before retaining in-house performance based on lack of private sector interest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation 3
rubrics_metrics.description: The Office of Federal Procurement Policy provide more definitive guidance on the use of CBD notices including what constitutes a sufficient response.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In the interim, Contracting Officers should be hesitant to use informational solicitation methodology in lieu of a formal solicitation process to avoid unnecessarily extending the acquisition process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation 4
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracting officers play a more active role in development of multifunctional solicitations and take the lead in developing a single solicitation document for the same CITA at different organizations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Advantages include lower overall acquisition and contract administration costs; however Contracting Officer must judge desirability of combining requirements which may favor larger firms versus policy to utilize small and disadvantaged businesses. Active early coordination with supported organizations is recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation 5
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracting personnel become totally familiar with directives relating to communications with groups interested in C/I Activities Program status or progress.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prevents premature release of information that could embarrass the command or attack system integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation 6
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracting Officers review existing organizational and staffing structure especially regarding establishing dedicated Service Branches or a separate Contract Administration Branch.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This assures contracting offices are prepared to process CITA requests effectively and efficiently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation 7
rubrics_metrics.description: Naval Supply Systems Command monitor field activity implementation efforts and provide additional resources commensurate with program growth.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Necessary to avoid worsening an already unsatisfactory workload situation; contracting offices should optimally organize existing resources to support projected program growth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation 8
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracting Officers reject statements of work that are not adequate for solicitation purposes and require resubmission rather than attempting to correct and update them after receipt.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contract negotiators must become familiar with elements of a good CITA work statement. Establish and maintain internal milestones; recognize unique CITA characteristics preclude attainment of existing Procurement Administrative Lead Time goals and provide realistic standards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation 9
rubrics_metrics.description: Naval Supply Systems Command and Naval Facilities Engineering Command definitize agreements as to which command will procure a specific service function.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This assists development of specialized expertise at contracting offices and enhances coordination, preparation, and submission of statements of work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation 10
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracting offices establish dedicated training programs centered around the key reference material noted in this research effort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Training should focus on the reference materials and procedures relevant to CITA contracting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation 11
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracting offices attempt to be more supportive of internal planning efforts of the Task Group.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Support ensures realistic milestones, accurate and complete statements of work, and maintenance of system integrity; coordinate schedules early in planning and before receipt of purchase request in contracting office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation 12
rubrics_metrics.description: Department of Defense and Navy directives be revised and clarified to conform with existing policy guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Clarification would enhance field contracting offices' ability to implement consistent policy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation 13
rubrics_metrics.description: Separate coverage of service contracting be included in the Defense Acquisition Regulation, including a distinct section on CITA Support Service Contracting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Would reduce confusion on issues such as clause usage inconsistencies, use of 8(a) set-asides, options and cost comparison process, methodologies for determining low private sector bid/offer, treatment of late submission of Government in-house estimate, and determining significant discrepancies in Government estimates. Incorporation of Firm Bid/Offer procedure (DAR Case 76-144) suggested.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation 14
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracting professionals should take aggressive action to assure the integrity of the system is above reproach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contracting Officers should self-assess actions for potential compromising positions and provide Standards of Conduct guidance to Task Group Chairpersons so all members understand duties and responsibilities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation 15
rubrics_metrics.description: In most instances, formal advertising methods should be used to accomplish the Cost Comparison for potential conversions of in-house to contractor performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Best accomplished by requiring submission of a performance-oriented statement of work detailing what is to be accomplished, not how it is to be done.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation 16
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracting offices should make maximum use of pre-bid/pre-proposal conferences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Important because many contractors may not know new concepts/procedures in CITA Support Service Contracting; contract negotiators must understand cost comparison process to answer questions intelligently at conferences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation 17
rubrics_metrics.description: To preserve equitability and integrity, Contracting Officers should consider the Government as simply another potential source of supply.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Procedures regarding submission of in-house cost estimate, negotiations, distribution of solicitation amendments, etc., should be the same for Government as for other potential contractors; treat Task Group Chairperson as equivalent to a private firm's president/GM and direct communications accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation 18
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracting Officers emphasize at pre-bid/pre-proposal conferences and by other methods that the additional Government costs to be incurred if a contract is awarded are award factors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Allows clear distinction between contractor quoted price and total cost to Government should a contract be awarded.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation 19
rubrics_metrics.description: Contract negotiators and personnel directly involved in a Bid or Public Opening should review existing CITA directives to ensure the process will be accomplished in a professional manner.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Review actions and procedures to secure professional handling of bid/public opening events.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation 20
rubrics_metrics.description: Contracting Officers review the Guidance in the Circular itself to assure they have a firm understanding of the appeals concept.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Significant for placing Contracting Officer role in both appeal and protest processes in proper perspective.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy: Rely on the Private Sector
rubrics_metrics.description: Where private sources are available, they should be looked to first to provide commercial or industrial goods and services needed by the Government.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Embedded in Circular's general policy: the Government should not compete with its citizens; private enterprise is primary source of national economic strength.

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy: Retain Certain Governmental Functions In-House
rubrics_metrics.description: Certain functions inherently governmental in nature must be performed in-house by Federal employees.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These include discretionary application of government authority, monetary transactions and entitlements, and in-house core R&D capabilities (with limits defined for non-core R&D).

rubrics_metrics.name: Policy: Aim for Economy; Use Cost Comparisons
rubrics_metrics.description: When private performance is feasible and no overriding factor requires in-house performance, rigorous comparison of contract costs versus in-house costs should be used to decide how the work will be done.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Cost Comparison Handbook is provided as a supplement to determine total cost to Government for each alternative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition: Government commercial or industrial activity
rubrics_metrics.description: An activity operated and managed by a Federal executive agency providing a product or service that could be obtained from a private source; must be separable and a regularly needed operational activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Representative listing provided in attachment; excludes one-time short-duration project activities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condition authorizing Government operation: No satisfactory commercial source
rubrics_metrics.description: A Government commercial or industrial activity can be authorized without a comparative cost analysis when it is demonstrated there is no private commercial source capable of providing the needed product/service or use of a private source would cause unacceptable delay/disruption.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agency must make all reasonable efforts to identify sources, including placing at least three CBD notices over 90 days (two notices over 30 days for urgent needs). Assistance from GSA, SBA, and Commerce is encouraged. Any claim of unacceptable delay/disruption must be specifically documented in terms of cost, time, and performance; classified program status or possibility of strike are not adequate justifications alone.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condition authorizing Government operation: National defense grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: A Government activity operated by military personnel may be justified when (a) activity/personnel are utilized or subject to deployment in direct combat support, (b) activity is essential for training in exclusively military skills, or (c) activity is needed for career progression/rotation bases for overseas assignments.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Depot/intermediate level maintenance justification requires criteria approved by Secretary of Defense and detailed explanation why private or contract GOCO cannot supply needed capability; approvals at assistant secretary level required.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condition authorizing Government operation: Higher cost
rubrics_metrics.description: A Government commercial or industrial activity may be authorized if a comparative cost analysis indicates the Government can provide the product/service at a lower total cost than private sector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Cost Comparisons must be prepared per paragraph 9 and the Cost Comparison Handbook.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost Comparisons: Common Ground Rule 1 - Same scope and performance
rubrics_metrics.description: Both Government and commercial cost figures must be based on the same scope of work and same level of performance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Requires a sufficiently precise work statement with performance standards that can be monitored for either mode of performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost Comparisons: Common Ground Rule 2 - Use standard cost factors
rubrics_metrics.description: Standard cost factors will be used as prescribed by the Cost Comparison Handbook and as supplemented by agencies for particular operations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must defend any variations in costing between cases.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost Comparisons: Common Ground Rule 3 - Aim at full cost
rubrics_metrics.description: Cost comparisons are to be aimed at full cost; all significant Government costs (including allocation of overhead and indirect costs) must be considered for direct performance and contract administration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Full cost accounting provides the basis for fair comparisons.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost Comparisons: Common Ground Rule 4 - Use prepriced/renewal options
rubrics_metrics.description: In solicitations for continuing workloads, solicitations should provide for prepriced options or renewal options for out-years unless inappropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Guards against 'buy-in' pricing; advantages include continuity, lower prices when contractor provides equipment/facilities, and reduced turbulence. Recompetition also guards against buy-ins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost Comparisons: Common Ground Rule 5 - Threshold for conducting studies
rubrics_metrics.description: Ordinarily, agencies should not conduct cost comparison studies for products/services estimated to be less than $100,000 in annual operating costs; activities below this threshold should be contracted unless justified otherwise.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If inadequate competition or unreasonable commercial prices suspected, a study may be conducted after reasonable efforts to obtain satisfactory commercial prices and develop competing sources.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cost Comparisons: Common Ground Rule 6 - Opportunity cost rate
rubrics_metrics.description: The cost comparison will use a rate of 10% per annum as the opportunity cost of capital investments and of net proceeds from potential sale of capital assets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prescribed by the Cost Comparison Handbook.

rubrics_metrics.name: Calculating Contract Costs
rubrics_metrics.description: The contract cost figure must be based on a binding firm bid or proposal, solicited in accordance with acquisition regulations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Bidders/offerors must be told that an in-house cost estimate is being developed and that a contract may or may not result depending on comparative costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of other Federal agency products/services
rubrics_metrics.description: Excess property and services available from other Federal agencies should be used in preference to new starts or contracts unless the needed product/service can be obtained more economically in the private sector.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When an agency has excess capacity reported under a formal program, other agencies may use it without further justification; otherwise use must be justified under paragraph 8 with comparative cost or solicitation to establish commercial costs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits and exclusions of Circular A-76
rubrics_metrics.description: Circular does not provide authority to enter into contracts, is not to be used to create employer-employee relationships, will not be used to contract out solely to meet personnel ceilings, and does not apply where contrary to law/treaty or to certain advisory consulting services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must follow applicable acquisition regulations and other legal constraints; special rules (e.g., A-109 for major system acquisitions) apply where relevant.
